# [AQUÆDICT]{.acronym-literal} Quality Prediction Models

::: {.floating-site-nav role="navigation" aria-label="Page navigation"}
[[AQUA]{.acronym-literal} Overview](authentication-quality-models.html){.floating-nav-link}
[Definitional Models](definitional-models.html){.floating-nav-link}
<!--Prediction Models](prediction-models.html){.floating-nav-link .active}-->
:::

[AQUÆDICT]{.acronym-literal} extends the [AQUA]{.acronym-literal} framework with **quality prediction models**. It does not introduce new definitional quality models. Instead, it builds on the existing definitional models **[AQUA-A]{.acronym-literal}**, **[AQUA-T]{.acronym-literal}**, and **[AQUA-S]{.acronym-literal}** [1] and operationalizes their quality factors and subfactors through prediction metrics.

The corresponding prediction models are **[AQUÆDICT-A]{.acronym-literal}** for Authenticator Quality Prediction, **[AQUÆDICT-T]{.acronym-literal}** for Authentication Technique Quality Prediction, and **[AQUÆDICT-S]{.acronym-literal}** for Authentication Solution Quality Prediction.

In other words, [AQUA]{.acronym-literal} defines **what quality means** for the respective authentication concepts, while [AQUÆDICT]{.acronym-literal} defines **how that quality can be predicted**.


::: {.callout-note}
## Current Scope

[AQUÆDICT]{.acronym-literal} is structured into three quality prediction models: **[AQUÆDICT-A]{.acronym-literal}** for Authenticators, **[AQUÆDICT-T]{.acronym-literal}** for Authentication Techniques, and **[AQUÆDICT-S]{.acronym-literal}** for Authentication Solutions.

At the current stage, **[AQUÆDICT-A]{.acronym-literal}** is developed in detail, including prediction metrics, normalization, and a worked demonstration. **[AQUÆDICT-T]{.acronym-literal}** and **[AQUÆDICT-S]{.acronym-literal}** are part of the prediction-model architecture but are not yet specified at the same level of detail.

Accordingly, the detailed material on this page currently focuses on **[AQUÆDICT-A]{.acronym-literal}**.
:::

# Prediction Methodology

The prediction methodology of [AQUÆDICT]{.acronym-literal} operationalizes the quality subfactors defined by [AQUA]{.acronym-literal} through corresponding **prediction metrics**. The methodology presented below is currently instantiated in detail for **[AQUÆDICT-A]{.acronym-literal}**, the Authenticator Quality Prediction Model.

## Prediction Metrics

For each quality subfactor considered by [AQUÆDICT-A]{.acronym-literal}, a **prediction metric** is defined. Depending on the subfactor, the metric either assigns an ordinal quality rank or directly yields a cardinal prediction value.

For an ordinal scale with $k$ quality levels,

$$
L_k = \{l_0 < l_1 < \dots < l_{k-1}\},
$$

the levels are ordered from the worst quality level $l_0$ to the best quality level $l_{k-1}$. For a quality subfactor $q$, the corresponding Authenticator-level quality prediction function is defined as

$$
Q_q : A \rightarrow L_{k_q},
$$

where $A$ is an Authenticator and $k_q$ is the number of quality levels defined for the respective subfactor.

## Normalization

To make ordinal prediction values comparable with cardinal prediction values, ordinal scales are normalized to the interval **[0, 1]** using an established approach from multi-criteria decision analysis [2].

$$
\operatorname{norm}(l_i) = \frac{i}{k_q - 1}
$$

The normalization assigns **0** to the worst quality level and **1** to the best quality level, independent of the number of levels defined for a particular quality subfactor. This provides a common numerical scale for comparing the resulting quality predictions.
